scope: Theorem 1.2 (Specialization in a polarized component) of the manuscript “A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences” (preprints/A-Conditional-Reduction-for-Algebraic-Kuga-Satake-Correspondences-September-10-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e59953bdc640de5f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2d. Assume that condition (i) or condition (ii) of Theorem 1.1 holds very generally in that component. Then every (S, h) in the component satisfies (1.2), with all the stipulated standard data on T(S). Here it suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart. In particular an input outside countably many proper algebraic subsets of the moduli component suffices. The witness cycles, abelian varieties, or surface covers need not vary in a family.
